  1                  AMENDED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF FROSTY MILLER

 2                                     I.    INTRODUCTION

 3   Q:   PLEASE STATE YOUR FULL NAME AND WHERE YOU LIVE.

 4   A:   My name is Foster “Frosty” Miller. I live just outside Pontotoc, Texas.

 5   Q:   HAVE YOU EVER TESTIFIED IN A PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF

 6        TEXAS ("PUC" OR "COMMISSION") PROCEEDING?

 7   A:   No, I have not.

 8   Q:   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU TESTIFYING?

 9   A:   I am testifying on behalf of myself, FVF Ranches Ltd., and PTX Ranches Ltd.

10                          II.   PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF TESTIMONY

11   Q:   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

12   A:   I am providing testimony as to the Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line

13        and to protect our private property and way of life that has sustained our family since the

14        1930’s.

15   Q:   ARE YOU FAMILIAR WITH THE STUDY AREA AS DESCRIBED BY THE

16        APPLICANT’S APPLICATION? IF YES, PLEASE EXPLAIN.

17   A:   Yes, very familiar as we have made our home and raised our family here since June 1,

18        1970.

19   Q:   WHERE IS THE MILLER PROPERTY LOCATED?

20   A:   Our property is located north of Pontotoc, and northeast along CR 501, approximately 5

21        miles. Applicants identified our property as Tract Nos. 1418, 1423, 4494.44, 4494.51;

22        affected by Links J6, K41.
 1                     III.   DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY AND LINE IMPACT

2    Q:   PLEASE TELL THE COMMISSIONERS ABOUT THE HISTORY OF YOUR

3         PROPERTY.

4    A:   My Grandfather, Vernon E Miller, began acquiring the ranch land in the early 1930’s. At

 5        his death, he transferred approximately 10,000+ to his four children.

 6        My father, Fay Miller, owned and operated his inherited part of the ranch from 1960,

 7        running cattle, sheep, and goats, plus irrigated farmland for peanuts, hay grazer and oats.

 8        Joining my Dad in 1970 were my brother and I, working on the ranch and raising our

 9        families.

10        Through the years, we were able to purchase and add to our ranch, adjoining properties,

11        which established the present-day Miller Ranch. Presently, we partner with our son and

12        daughter in running the ranching business and a deer hunting operation. Our lives continue

13        to revolve around our ranch and maintain it in a manner that would be sustainable for

14        generations to come.

15   Q:   WHAT ARE YOUR CONCERNS IF THE PROJECT WERE TO USE YOUR

16        PROPERTY?

17   A:   We are concerned that should this project proceed on or even near our property, it would

18        be a total disruption of our lives. The property would be devalued by a minimum of 50%,

19        which would affect our health, and that of the animals and wildlife. The activities and

20        privacy that we have enjoyed for 56 years could be totally disrupted. We are further

21        concerned that because of this project, our ability to maintain a sustainable livelihood

22        would be totally negated.

23
  1   Q:   PLEASE EXPLAIN THE RESIDENTIAL USE OF YOUR PROPERTY.

 2   A:   Our home has been the headquarters of the ranch for the entirety of our family ownership.

 3        We have lived in this home since June 1, 1970, and continue to do so. Both our son and

 4        daughter were raised in this location from birth.

 5   Q:   PLEASE DESCRIBE THE RECREATIONAL AND WILDLIFE ASPECTS OF

 6        YOUR PROPERTY.

 7   A:   We have approximately 970 acres of high-fenced property that joins Ranch Road 501,

 8        which is used for guided deer hunts for whitetail deer, axis, black Buck antelope, turkey,

 9        dove, and feral hogs. The remaining property is low-fenced and is leased for seasonal

10        hunting of deer, turkey, hogs, and dove.

11   Q:   HOW IS THE PROPERTY USED FOR FARMING/HUNTING/RANCHING

12        ACTIVITIES?

13   A:   Our ranch entails approximately 500+ acres of farmland that has improved grasses of Klein

14        and Willman Love Grass that are used for deferred rotational grazing and the production

15        of hay. Presently, we are a commercial cattle operation with Angus cows bred to Charolais

16        Bulls. We run an intensive hunting operation, which is described in the previous question.

17   Q:   ARE THERE ANY WATER WELLS IMPACTED BY LINK J6 OR K41? IF SO,

18        PLEASE DESCRIBE THEIR GENERAL LOCATIONS AND USAGE.

19   A:   Yes, the proposed J6 line goes over two wells in our pastures, one is directly across from

20        our home, south of RR 501. This well is used for one of our hunting cabins and to water

21        livestock and wildlife, and it can serve as an alternative to our home and corrals. The other

22        is for livestock and wildlife. K41 would be directly affecting 2,300-gallon irrigation wells

23        as well.
 1    Q:   ARE THERE ANY HABITABLE STRUCTURES ON THE PROPERTY THAT

2         WILL BE AFFECTED BY LINK J6 OR K41?

3    A:   Yes, our home and residence for the last 56 years may be within 500 feet of the centerline

4         of the proposed link. Also, possibly within that range would be one of our hunting cabins

5         that has been used seasonally since 1972.

6    Q:   ARE THERE ANY ISSUES WITH J6 OR K41 IN GENERAL THAT YOU

 7        BELIEVE SHOULD BE ADDRESSED BY THE COMMISSION?

 8   A:   J6 and K41 directly affect our home, our water wells, and our high fence deer operation

 9        and livestock. In other words, at our age, our total lifestyle and ranch income will be

10        disrupted. We would likely have to move from a home and lifestyle that we have known

11        most of our lives, for 56 years. Plus, the value of our land would be reduced to at least half

12        of its present-day value.

13   Q:   ARE THERE ANY ISSUES WITH ANY OTHER LINKS THAT YOU BELIEVE

14        SHOULD BE ADDRESSED BY THE COMMISSION?

15   A:   K41 goes very near our small town of Pontotoc. We have mostly an elderly population

16        remaining in Pontotoc. A large transmission line near their homes would be a total

17        disruption of their lives.

18   Q:   DO YOU HAVE ANY OBJECTIONS OR SUGGESTIONS REGARDING THE

19        BEST-MEETS ROUTE?

20   A:   At this time, we do not oppose the Applicants’ best-meets route; however, we reserve the

21        right to change our position.

22
  1                      IV.     CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS

 2   Q:   HOW WOULD YOU SUMMARIZE YOUR POSITION IN THIS PROCEEDING

 3        REGARDING ROUTING?

 4   A:   As ranchers and private property owners for all of our married life, we cannot imagine the

 5        intrusion and necessity for this gigantic project to totally disrupt the lives of so very many

 6        people, and ruin the livelihood and beauty of this beautiful hill country. I am a rancher and

 7        have been a real estate broker since 1985, an agent since 1983, and have marketed many

 8        ranches in this area. After consulting with other brokers in the area, we are deeply

 9        concerned that this project will devalue our land by a minimum of 50%. We have worked

10        all our lives to maintain this ranch, so it would be of value to our children to inherit and

11        continue with our family tradition of living and loving this land that our ancestors and

12        ourselves have worked so very hard to acquire and retain for future generations.

13   Q:   DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR TESTIMONY?

14   A:   Yes.
